decisions.reason: As a pharmacy-oriented supplement range adjacent to the firm’s OTC and consumer-health capabilities, it is close enough to existing knowledge that management would likely keep it and improve the line rather than exit quickly.
A skin-and-hair supplement is relatively far from the firm’s core pharmaceutical strengths and sits in a crowded category, so limited distinctive learning advantages make discontinuation more likely.

A joint-health supplement fits better with the firm’s health-focused pharmacy channel and therapeutic positioning, giving it enough relatedness to existing knowledge to justify continued market presence.

A mushroom-based immune supplement is the most novel and least anchored in the firm’s established pharmaceutical knowledge base, so management is more likely to reallocate resources if performance is not clearly strong.

A generic blood-pressure medicine is highly aligned with the firm’s core development, manufacturing, regulatory, and quality capabilities, and those absorptive-capacity advantages make retention likely despite the earlier valsartan issue.

An OTC migraine triptan tablet is closely related to the firm’s prescription-to-OTC pharmaceutical know-how and pharmacy relationships, so management would usually keep it and learn from early sales before considering withdrawal.
